advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Drop the stray {"project": "DIG"} from the reconciler case (or move the shared fixture to only add a section-valid key), since 'project' is not a reconciler-section key.
evidence: src/rebar/_config_schema.py:689-694 the 'jira' section defines 'project' but the reconciler section (lines 675-688) has no 'project' key
The assertion only checks `key not in out.get(section, {})`, so the stray 'project' key never affects the pass/fail outcome
advisory.finding: In test_a_config_still_setting_the_key_loads_and_drops_it, the reconciler-section case passes an extra {"project": "DIG"} key, but 'project' is not a valid key of the reconciler section (it belongs to [jira]); it is silently accepted only because coerce_sparse warns-and-ignores unknown keys under non-strict default. The added key does nothing useful for this test and could mislead a reader into thinking reconciler.project is a real setting.

advisory.finding: The removed env twins REBAR_JIRA_RESOLVED_STATUSES / REBAR_RECONCILER_RESOLVED_STATUSES have no BEHAVIORAL test exercising the actual env-tombstone path (raise_or_warn_env via load_config) with the env var SET; coverage stops at the registry-level assertion tombstone_for('env', name).behavior == 'warn'. The direct precedent cited in the code comment (REBAR_CODE_HEALTH_ENABLED) does have such a behavioral test, so the contract 'a set env twin warns and does not abort' is left unverified for this change.
scenarios: A future edit to raise_or_warn_env's skip/startswith logic silently drops the warning for these env vars; the registry-only test still passes

advisory.suggested_fix: In test_config_resolved_statuses_removal.py, add a parametrized test over REMOVED_ENV using monkeypatch.setenv + load_config (or raise_or_warn_env(os.environ)) under caplog.at_level(WARNING, logger='rebar'), asserting no RemovedInputError and that the message contains the env name and 'was removed in'.
